question: I bought two shirts for ₹1,200. I sold the first shirt at a loss of 7% and the second at a profit of 28%. If I made neither a loss nor a profit overall, find the cost price (in ₹) of the first shirt.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When overall profit or loss is 0%, the monetary loss on one item equals the monetary profit on the other.

⇒ Loss % × CP₁ = Profit % × CP₂

⇒ 7 × CP₁ = 28 × CP₂

⇒ Ratio of CP₁ : CP₂ = 28 : 7 = 4 : 1

⇒ CP₁ = (4/5) × 1200 = 960

**∴ The correct answer is ₹960.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total Cost Price of two shirts = ₹1,200

Loss on the 1st shirt = 7%

Profit on the 2nd shirt = 28%

Overall transaction resulted in neither profit nor loss (0%).

**Method Used:**

We can solve this efficiently using the rule of Alligation by finding the ratio of their Cost Prices.
